slides.title: The agentic loop is the unit of work

elements.text: The agentic loop is the unit of work
The prompt, the files it points at, and the results of the tools that already ran.
The model emits a request for a tool: bash, read, edit.
The tool runs: tests, command output, re-read state.
REPEAT - every step is conditioned on what the last one returned. One user prompt is many model calls and many tool executions, not a single request.
An agent is a loop plus a trust boundary, not a smarter completion. The model proposes; the harness executes.

slides.title: The model proposes, the harness executes

elements.text: The model proposes, the harness executes
The model emits a request such as Bash("pytest"). It proposes; it does not execute.
The Claude Code harness resolves the request, checks permissions, and executes it.
The tool runs where you are. The repository never leaves disk: Claude pulls slices of it on demand.
The tool_result goes back into the model's context. The harness owns the loop, the context and the permissions.

The agentic loop, not the prompt, is the unit of work.

slides.title: A tool request is a proposal, not an action

elements.text: A tool request is a proposal, not an action
The permission layer sits between intent and execution: a tool request needs approval before it runs.
This is what students get wrong: the model never acts on the world directly. The harness does, and it can refuse.
Context grows with every step, and is then compacted.

Every memory creation is a decision about what gets re-read forever. Every permanent token is rent paid at the start of every session. Stale memory is worse than none, because it actively misleads. Treat memory like code and keep it in version control.

How the agent should perform a task. A folder whose description controls discovery and whose body holds the procedure. Model-invoked when the description matches the task, or user-invoked with /<skill-name>.
Which external data and actions the agent can reach, through a standard protocol.
What happens automatically at a lifecycle event: session start, user prompt, tool call, tool result, stop.
How the extensions are packaged and distributed: installation, versioning, namespacing, team reuse.
A skill decides how, MCP reaches outside, a hook enforces, a plugin distributes. Each attaches at a different point in the agent loop.

slides.title: MCP: one protocol for external capability

elements.text: MCP: one protocol for external capability
MCP (Model Context Protocol) connects the agent to external services through a standard protocol. Before MCP exists: NxM implementations.

A call is almost identical to a local tool: same name, description and typed schema, same call-and-return contract, because it just runs in another process. The protocol carries the call while the agent still decides whether to make it.

slides.title: Name the problem, then pick the mechanism

elements.text: Name the problem, then pick the mechanism

The four extension mechanisms are explicitly non-interchangeable, and the lecture ends with this classification exercise. A skill decides how, MCP reaches outside, a hook enforces, a plugin distributes.

slides.title: Three things to carry out of Lecture 2

elements.text: Three things to carry out of Lecture 2
One user prompt expands into many model calls and many tool executions; the agentic loop is the unit of work.
The model proposes, the harness executes, and the harness owns context, permissions and memory.
Skill, MCP, Hook and Plugin solve four different problems and must not be confused. Memory is rented context: write only what you want re-read forever.
